group.title: Staff lavatory used as storage
group.note: The boxed-in actual toilet, closer background and three wedding-assistant poses.

hotel_staff_lavatory_move_boxes.speaker: hotel_wedding_assistant
text: Oh! Of course. Just a moment.

text.desc: She begins removing boxes. You help clear a space around the toilet. For the first time in what feels like hours, you can actually see the seat.
She stops. A red ribbon is stretched across the toilet lid. Attached to it is an auction tag: LOT 58 — STAFF TOILET. SOLD — COLLECTION AFTER CEREMONY. DO NOT TEST.

text: He sold the room to us for storage and the toilet to somebody else.
I'm terribly sorry. The buyer apparently insists on receiving it in its original condition.

text.desc: She carefully replaces one of the boxes.

text: I really think you should find the wedding organizer.

text.desc: You look at the toilet. It looks perfectly functional. That somehow makes everything worse.

choices.text: IGNORE THE AUCTION TAG AND TRY TO USE THE TOILET ANYWAY.
FIND THE WEDDING ORGANIZER IN THE BALLROOM.
RETURN TO THE BOILER ROOM AND TRY ANOTHER TOILET.

hotel_staff_lavatory_storage.speaker: hotel_wedding_assistant

text.desc: You open the staff lavatory. An actual toilet sits beneath a mountain of boxes marked WEDDING FAVORS.
An assistant is stacking place cards on the cistern.

text: Oh! Are you here for the favors?
The room was sold to us as overflow storage. The auctioneer called it a convenience facility.

text.desc: You look at the boxes. They are very convenient for someone else.

text: There’s another lavatory off the bridal dressing room upstairs. The organizer has the key.
Please don’t disturb the boxes. They’re sorted by table number.

choices.text: COULD YOU MOVE THESE BOXES? I REALLY NEED TO USE THAT TOILET.
FIND THE WEDDING ORGANIZER IN THE BALLROOM.
LEAVE THE BOXES AND CHECK THE ENGINEERS’ LAVATORY.

hotel_staff_lavatory_temporary_use_permi.speaker: hotel_wedding_assistant

text.desc: You remove the SOLD ribbon and lift the toilet lid. Finally. You reach toward your belt.

text: Wait! You'll need a Temporary Use Permit.
To issue one, I first need to verify that the toilet flushes.
No! Testing a sold toilet requires a Temporary Use Permit!
Well, there's an exception form. The wedding organizer can sign it.

text.desc: She places her clipboard on the toilet seat.
You stare at the toilet. Two feet away. Completely functional. Entirely unavailable.

choices.text: YES. WHERE CAN I FIND THE WEDDING ORGANIZER?
LEAVE THE PAPERWORK BEHIND AND RETURN TO THE BOILER ROOM.
